profile.name: Aaron Guckian
profile.current_role: Former executive director of the Rhode Island Dental Association
profile.bio: Aaron Guckian narrowly leads Elaine Pelino in the 2026 Republican primary for Governor of Rhode Island, with a recount pending, and was endorsed by the state Republican Party. He previously served as director of advance for Governor Donald Carcieri, worked as a development officer at the Rhode Island Foundation and led the Rhode Island Dental Association until November 2025.
profile.notes: He describes himself as a compassionate conservative, but no specific policy positions or campaign website could be verified. The Republican nomination is subject to a pending recount.

profile.name: Eunice Lehmacher
profile.bio: Eunice Lehmacher is a social worker and counselor who was born in Lexington, Missouri, and campaigns from Central, South Carolina. She won the Democratic nomination for SC-3 in June 2026.

platform.point: Aims to lower high prices for working families, small businesses and seniors.
Wants to increase access to doctors and hospitals.
Supports investing in childcare as a workforce investment.
Seeks to restore housing opportunity and affordability.
Raises surveillance and privacy concerns about data center expansion.
Favors peaceful solutions over military conflict.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: supports access and public funding of reproductive care for low-income women, while calling for safety standards on abortion pills.

profile.notes: Her issues page gives headings with few specifics, so most scores are left null. Ballotpedia blocked access this pass, so the liberty evidence was confirmed only through a secondary summary of her survey answers.

profile.name: Courtney McClain
profile.bio: Courtney McClain is a Spartanburg native with a journalism degree from the University of South Carolina and a political science master's from Howard University. She led the South Carolina NAACP Youth and College Division and held fellowships with the Congressional Black Caucus Institute and the Clyburn Fellow Program. At 25, she won the Democratic nomination for SC-4.

platform.point: Prioritizes building more affordable housing.
Says affordable health care should be accessible to everyone.
Aims to reduce everyday costs for Upstate families.
Wants to manage the Upstate's rapid population growth.
Has advocated on reproductive health, public education, voting rights and criminal justice reform.

welfare.evidence: Describes affordable healthcare as a right for all.

profile.name: John Peterson
profile.current_role: North Charleston Convention Center employee and former mathematician
profile.bio: John Peterson is a former mathematician who now works full-time at the North Charleston Convention Center. He describes himself as a Donald Trump Republican and has canvassed as a volunteer for Trump's campaigns. He is the Republican nominee challenging Jim Clyburn in SC-6.

platform.point: Wants to address the national debt and rein in federal spending.
Supports the Department of Government Efficiency effort.
Aims to lower gas, grocery and insurance prices.
Opposes a proposed $5,000 dividend to Americans, citing its cost.

economy.evidence: Calls for cutting federal spending and backs government-efficiency cuts.

profile.name: John Vincent
profile.bio: John Vincent is the Democratic nominee for South Carolina's 7th Congressional District. His campaign says he served 20 years in the U.S. Navy and later built a small business. He says he will not accept corporate PAC donations.

platform.point: End tariffs, protect Social Security, raise wages and make home ownership more attainable.
Restore small-business programs, give farmers stable trade policy and expand career-focused training.
Keep rural hospitals open and preserve health care tax credits.
Keep commitments made to veterans, teachers and first responders.
Support term limits, a ban on congressional stock trading, limits on dark money and a balanced budget.

economy.evidence: Wants to end tariffs while also calling for higher wages and budget discipline.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to protect Social Security and health care tax credits and keep rural hospitals open.

profile.notes: Hometown and details of his business are not stated on the campaign site.

profile.name: Darline Graham
profile.bio: Darline Graham was appointed to the U.S. Senate by Governor Henry McMaster in July 2026 to fill the seat left vacant by the death of her brother, Senator Lindsey Graham, and is the first woman to represent South Carolina in the Senate. She previously worked at the South Carolina Vocational Rehabilitation Department and served as Commissioner of the South Carolina Commission for the Blind from 2019. A native of Central, South Carolina, she holds degrees from the College of Charleston and South Carolina State University.

platform.point: Cosponsors bills expanding U.S.-Israel defense cooperation and countering campus antisemitism.
Backs the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026.
Cosponsors bills on mandatory E-Verify, ending sanctuary cities and limiting birthright citizenship.
Cosponsors bills restricting abortion medication and permanently barring federal abortion funding.
Backs national concealed-carry reciprocity and removing suppressors from National Firearms Act rules.
Pledges to defend women's and girls' sports under Title IX.

liberty.evidence: Cosponsors abortion restrictions and backs limits on transgender athletes, while supporting looser gun regulation.

immigration.evidence: Cosponsors bills limiting birthright citizenship, mandating E-Verify, defunding sanctuary cities and expanding 287(g).

foreign.evidence: Cosponsors bills deepening U.S.-Israel defense cooperation and introduced Russia sanctions legislation.

profile.notes: Input lists no member_of_congress record although she is a sitting appointed senator, so the Commons official portrait (U.S. Congress public domain) was used. Liberty score is new, from her official releases on abortion, guns and women's sports.

profile.name: Charlie Hatcher
profile.bio: Charlie Hatcher is a dairy farmer and livestock veterinarian who served as Tennessee's Commissioner of Agriculture from 2019 to 2025 under Governor Bill Lee. He holds an animal science degree from Middle Tennessee State University and a veterinary degree from the University of Tennessee, and has founded several businesses. He won the 2026 Republican primary for the 5th District, defeating incumbent Andy Ogles.

platform.point: Describes himself as a pro-gun candidate who will defend Second Amendment rights.
Campaigns as a pro-life candidate.
Pledges to back President Trump, whom he calls the most consequential president of his lifetime.
Says he will bring a farmer's work ethic and common sense to Washington.

liberty.evidence: Campaign identifies him as pro-life (abortion) and pro-gun (guns), leaning toward community norms on abortion and individual choice on guns.

profile.notes: Campaign site offers only brief themes and no detailed issues page.

profile.name: Chaz Molder
profile.bio: Chaz Molder has been mayor of Columbia, Tennessee, since 2018, when he became the youngest mayor in the city's history; he was re-elected in 2022. His campaign highlights balanced city budgets and infrastructure and education investments during his tenure. He is the Democratic nominee for Tennessee's 5th District.

platform.point: Supports banning members of Congress from trading individual stocks.
Pledges to make healthcare, housing and groceries more affordable for Tennessee families.
Backs workers' right to organize and stronger labor protections.
Wants to lower healthcare costs, expand coverage, invest in preventive care and keep rural hospitals open.

economy.evidence: Supports workers' organizing rights, stronger labor protections and action on the cost of housing, groceries and healthcare.

welfare.evidence: Calls for broadening health insurance coverage, lowering costs and supporting rural hospitals.
